intro.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: I'm Wren. I keep the notes for Cedar Hollow Station.
Walk around. If something doesn't fit, look closer — the tablet will keep it.

observations.title: Granite Knob
observations.text: This is the high point of Cedar Hollow. Everything I can see leans away from the knob.
observations.prompt: Bare rock and a thin wind. The valley is a bowl beneath the mountain.

observations.title: High Look
observations.text: From the overlook, Granite Knob is the high point. The whole hollow tilts downhill toward the south.
observations.prompt: The valley falls away beneath you. Ridges, woods, and a silver thread of creek.

observations.title: Westface Slope
observations.text: Water from the western slope drains toward Pine Creek. Nothing here holds a rainstorm in place.
observations.prompt: The ground is steep and scored with tiny rills. Last night's rain left them shining.

observations.title: Pine Creek
observations.text: Pine Creek is pulling water from the west and carrying it southeast, into the hollow.
observations.prompt: The creek is loud and tea-colored. Current runs clearly downhill.

observations.title: Alder Woods
observations.text: The forest floor is damp, but the woods sit above the creek. Water here still has somewhere lower to go.
observations.prompt: Ferns and leaf litter. The ground slopes, faintly, toward the sound of water.

observations.title: Mirror Pond
observations.text: Mirror Pond collects Pine Creek from the northwest, then lets it continue south. A pause, not an ending.
observations.prompt: The pond is higher than usual. An inlet on one side, an outlet on the other.

observations.title: Willow Bench
observations.text: This bench is lower than the woods around it. Water would linger here after a hard rain.
observations.prompt: Soft ground. Willows. A faint wrack line of sticks from last night.

observations.title: Willow Reach
observations.text: High-water marks on the willows. Last night's runoff ended up downstream of the pond.
observations.prompt: The reach is still swollen. Grass lies flattened in the direction of flow.

observations.title: Research Station
observations.text: The station sits on a shoulder above the hollow — high enough to stay dry, close enough to watch the drainage.
observations.prompt: A small cabin, a rain gauge, and a porch that looks west into the valley.

conclusion.prompt: Trace last night's water. Tap the places you actually walked, in the order water would travel.
conclusion.successText: That's the story. Rain on Westface Slope ran to Pine Creek, paused in Mirror Pond, then pushed out Willow Reach. That's why the water jumped downstream.
conclusion.uphillHint: Water doesn't climb. Check the high ground against the low ground in your notes.
conclusion.incompleteHint: Your tablet still has blank pages. Walk a little more before we trace the path.
conclusion.unobservedHint: You can only trace places you've actually stood. Go see the land first.

completeJournalEntry.title: Where the water went
completeJournalEntry.text: Runoff from Westface Slope fed Pine Creek, filled Mirror Pond, and continued downstream to Willow Reach.
